clue.text: Great bloke on pole, the main controller

indicators.note: on here means the great bloke is set after the pole letter, sitting on it

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for the south pole
top means first-rate, great
cock is old British slang for a man or chap

explanation.surface: A tremendous fellow up a pole is the chief in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: A water main is the pipe the valve shuts off, which is why 'main controller' reads as a person in charge but is a plumbing fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: This valve shuts off or regulates the flow of water from the supply pipe, so it controls the mains.

clue.text: I'm an adult wandering in state bordering Kerala

indicators.note: wandering means moving about aimlessly, so these letters are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A grown-up traveller roams through a part of southern India.
explanation.definitionFit: This Indian state lies on the south-east of the peninsula, sharing a border with its western neighbour Kerala.

clue.text: Wok expert given a comprehensive fix

parts.note: a wok is a kind of pan used in Chinese cooking
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A master of stir-fry cooking is handed a thorough remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A cure-all is a remedy for every ill, a fix that covers everything.

clue.text: Open delivering Carnoustie's fifth green

indicators.note: the fifth letter of the word Carnoustie is taken, counting C-A-R-N-O

parts.note: vert is the heraldic word for green

explanation.surface: The Open golf championship held at Carnoustie, played on its fifth green.
explanation.walkthrough: Carnoustie is a Scottish golf course that hosts the Open championship, so 'Open' and 'green' look like golf; 'delivering' is a link. VERT is the heraldic name for green.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done in plain view, not hidden, is unconcealed and public.

clue.text: Football stand quiet after start of game

indicators.note: after places the letter for quiet behind the letters for the kick-off

parts.note: KO is short for kick-off, the start of a football game
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: The crowd in a football stand falls silent once the match has begun.
explanation.walkthrough: KO stands for kick-off, how a football match starts. The Kop is the famous terrace at Anfield, Liverpool's ground; the name is used for similar stands elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is given to a steep terrace of standing spectators at a British football ground, most famously Liverpool's.

clue.text: Where schoolchildren snitch?

definitions.meaning: pupils are placed within a class, a form in British schools
to snitch is to tell on someone to the authorities

explanation.definitionFit: Pupils sit within a class, called a form in British schools; and to snitch is to tell tales on someone.

clue.text: One's in the subcontinent — north-west of here?

indicators.note: in tells us the word for one's goes within the country's name

parts.note: the Indian subcontinent is named after India
one's written in letters, the possessive turned into ones

explanation.surface: Someone is in India, and wonders which country lies to its south-east.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a riddle: 'here' is a place with the subcontinent to its north-west, the island nation lying south-east of it. 'in' places the one's letters inside the country's name, after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Southeast Asian archipelago country lies south-east of India, so India sits north-west of it.

clue.text: Hot food, so blow

definitions.meaning: a hot piece of battered, deep-fried food
to blow money is to squander it, to waste it away

explanation.definitionFit: A battered, fried morsel is served hot; and to waste money gradually is to squander it away.

clue.text: King, having captured us city, put feet up

indicators.note: having captured means the word for king holds the city letters inside it

parts.note: rex is Latin for king, as in royal signatures
LA is Los Angeles, a city in the US

explanation.surface: A monarch, having taken an American city, rests his weary feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'us' stands for the US, so the city is LA, held inside REX.
explanation.definitionFit: To put your feet up is to take your ease and unwind.

clue.text: Workers in need of answer get the last word

parts.note: men are workers, as in management and men

explanation.surface: Labourers who need a reply get to have the final say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in need of' is a link: the workers need the answer letter, which goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: The word ends a prayer or hymn, so it is literally the closing word.

clue.text: Strange feeling a bit attached to one, beginning to eulogise shoe!

parts.note: ESP, extrasensory perception, is an uncanny sixth sense
a drill is the tool a bit is attached to, so 'one' refers to the drill

indicators.note: beginning to means only the first letter of the word eulogise is taken

explanation.surface: Someone praises a shoe with a weird sensation and an odd attachment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit attached to one' reads as a small amount of attachment, but 'one' is what a bit is fitted to: A DRILL. 'beginning to' takes E from eulogise.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a light canvas shoe with a rope sole, from the Pyrenees.

clue.text: A prickly thing to go without god among Britain's extremists

indicators.note: among means the middle pieces sit inside the outer letters of the next word
extremists means the first and last letters of the word Britain

parts.note: to lack something is to go without it
Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: Going godless among British radicals is a thorny business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Britain's extremists' gives B and N, the first and last letters of Britain, which hold LACK and THOR.
explanation.definitionFit: The sloe bush is a thorny shrub, so it is a spiky plant.

clue.text: Play: it starts "in the beginning" by word of introduction

parts.note: the Old Testament, OT, opens with Genesis: in the beginning God created
hello is a greeting used when meeting someone

explanation.surface: A drama whose opening line is a famous phrase, followed by a greeting.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation is the first words of Genesis, so 'it' is the Old Testament, OT. 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragedy of the Moor of Venice is a stage play.

clue.text: Test a number of groups in biology

parts.note: to tax someone is to test or strain them

explanation.surface: A biology exam asks about several categories of organisms.
explanation.definitionFit: Taxonomic categories such as genus or species are plural units of classification for living things.

clue.text: German reversed round a vehicle, it's plain to see

indicators.note: round means the reversed name goes around the other pieces
reversed tells us the German name is read from right to left

parts.note: Hans is a typical German man's name
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A German man backs his car around and admires the flat scenery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversed' gives SNAH, which 'round' wraps around the vehicle. 'it's' and 'to see' are links, and 'plain' is the flat grassland, not 'obvious'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical grassland is open flat country, a grassy expanse.

clue.text: What's needed when jumper in such a state?

definitions.text: What's needed when jumper in such a state?

parts.words: What's needed when jumper in such a state?
parts.note: a worn-out sweater calls for a replacement; that phrase is also the name of a US state

explanation.definitionFit: A fresh pullover is what a tatty one demands, and the phrase also names an American state on the Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Emphasise why off work?

definitions.meaning: to emphasise a point is to lay weight on it
workplace anxiety is a common reason for sick leave

explanation.definitionFit: To lay weight on a point is to accent it; and nervous strain is a common cause of sick leave.

clue.text: Southern bird over promontory — serious nature!

parts.note: a tern is a seabird
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: A bird from the south perched above a headland looks very grave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is a link in this down clue: S, then TERN, then NESS from top to bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Severity of manner is a grave, unsmiling disposition.

clue.text: Poor dog! Not many get restraining order

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel or worthless dog
few means not many

explanation.surface: A pitiful hound, rarely seen, is put under a court injunction.
explanation.definitionFit: A rule that people stay indoors after a set hour restricts their movement, so it is an order of restraint.

clue.text: The high road, where insect settled

parts.note: a fly is an insect
over means finished, settled and done with

explanation.surface: A road on stilts, where a bug came to rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'where' is a link joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An elevated road crossing above another is a raised carriageway.

clue.text: Might etrol be?

parts.note: the misspelt fuel has lost its first letter, its leader, so it is free of that lead

explanation.definitionFit: Unleaded fuel contains no tetraethyl lead; here the fuel's opening letter has also gone.

clue.text: Charlie seeks articles in fashion

indicators.note: in tells us the articles go within the word for a fashion

parts.note: a fad is a passing fashion
the and a are the definite and indefinite articles

explanation.surface: A man named Charlie goes looking for clothing pieces in the fashion pages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charlie' looks like a name, but in British slang a charlie is a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie is British slang for a silly person, a dimwit.

clue.text: Dairy product needs wife to call for attention

parts.note: hey is a shout to get someone's attention

explanation.surface: A milky item needs a married woman to shout out for notice.
explanation.definitionFit: The watery liquid left when milk curdles in cheesemaking is a by-product of the dairy.

clue.text: Might one be up on this drug?

definitions.text: Might one be up on this
definitions.meaning: one rides mounted on this animal

explanation.definitionFit: A rider sits up on the animal; and it is street slang for heroin.

clue.text: High cost of living holds single relative back

indicators.note: holds means the word for living has the other letters within it

parts.note: extant means still existing, alive

indicators.note: back means the single letter and relative are read from right to left together

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
bro is short for brother

explanation.surface: The steep cost of living keeps a lone relative from moving forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the single letter and the relative together into ORBI, which 'holds' sets inside the word for living after its first two letters. 'cost of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Prices far beyond reason are steep, unreasonably large.

clue.text: Note always turning up — rare one?

parts.note: B is a musical note

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: ever means always

explanation.surface: A musical note that keeps rising: is it an unusual one?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like the definition but gives B; the definition is 'rare one?', since this long note is seldom used in modern music.
explanation.definitionFit: The double whole note is a sustained note seldom written in modern scores.

clue.text: Wine has colour which is superior to body

parts.note: Graves is a Bordeaux wine
a tone is a shade of colour

explanation.surface: A Bordeaux has a tint that is better than its body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'superior to body' reads as tasting notes on the wine, but means placed above a buried body. 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A headstone stands above a buried corpse, so it is physically over the body.

clue.text: Is his brain left redundant?

indicators.note: redundant means the letter for left is dropped as surplus

parts.note: loaf is rhyming slang for head (loaf of bread), as in use your loaf

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone's mind has been put out of work.
explanation.walkthrough: In British rhyming slang 'loaf' (of bread) means head, or brain. The whole clue also describes a lout who never uses his head.
explanation.definitionFit: A clumsy, stupid person seems never to use his head.

clue.text: Prime minister is in the garden

definitions.meaning: the biblical paradise where Adam and Eve lived

explanation.definitionFit: Sir Anthony of that name led Britain in the 1950s; and the biblical paradise was a garden.

clue.text: Fancy fish to sell down the river

parts.note: to fancy a horse is to back it, to bet
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: Someone with a taste for fish ends up double-crossing a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: To sell someone down the river is to be treacherous to them.

clue.text: Cryptic finished, as you'd expect one to be?

definitions.text: as you'd expect one to be

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling, obscured, so the letters are disguised by rearrangement

explanation.surface: A solver has completed a cryptic and found it as hard as expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cryptic' looks like the noun for the puzzle, but it signals the rearrangement of 'finished'; 'one' in the definition is a cryptic crossword.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic puzzle is expected to be devilishly difficult.
